maternal fat intake during pregnancy is associated to the risk of pregnancy complications and poor birth outcomes.
maternal fat composition is a risk factor for pregnancy complications and poor fetal growth and that maternal long chain polyunsaturate fatty acids status is associated with improved birth outcome.

the role of maternal lipid metabolism on fetal growth and long term health.
the role of maternal fats on fetal growth, development, pregnancy complications and long term health.
the effects of maternal lipids on the long term health of mother and child.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal fat intake during pregnancy is an important determinant of pregnancy outcomes.
maternal lipids during gestation play a key role in the health of the mother and the fetus.

a high intake of saturated fatty acids during pregnancy is associated to adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas a high maternal intake of long chain polyunsaturates fatty acids is associated with improved birth outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal fat composition during pregnancy is a critical factor that determines pregnancy outcome, fetal growth, development and health in later life.
maternal lipids play a key role in fetal development and long-term health of the offspring and therefore should be taken into account in clinical practice.
the quality and quantity of maternal lipids is a modifiable risk factor for pregnancy complications and poor birth outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal diet should be carefully planned during pregnancy to prevent pregnancy complications and to improve fetal growth and development.
maternal fat composition plays an important role in fetal growth and development.
maternal lipid metabolism is critical during pregnancy for the health of the fetus and the long term health of offspring.
